title: Separate the smooth and radicial parts of an affine group quotient
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $H,J$ be smooth connected affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-connected-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $q:H\to J$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism. Write $N=\ker q$ for the scheme-theoretic kernel and $L=N_{\mathrm{red}}$ for its reduced closed subscheme, obtained by dividing each affine coordinate ring by its nilradical [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Then $L$ is a smooth closed normal subgroup of $H$, and the fppf sheaf quotient $P=H/L$ is a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type. Here fppf quotient means the sheafification of $A\mapsto H(A)/L(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras. The quotient map $a:H\to P$ is a smooth faithfully flat finitely presented $L$-torsor, meaning that $(h,l)\mapsto(h,hl)$ identifies $H\times_k L$ with $H\times_P H$. There is a finite faithfully flat radicial homomorphism $b:P\to J$ with $q=b\circ a$ and kernel $N/L$; radicial means universally injective, or equivalently injective on points valued in every algebraically closed extension field. If a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme $A$ of finite type acts on $H$ and $J$ by group automorphisms and $q$ is equivariant, then the action on $H$ preserves $L$ as a subgroup scheme and descends to an action on $P$ by group automorphisms for which both $a$ and $b$ are equivariant. Neither $N$ nor $L$ is required to be connected, and $N$ need not be smooth.

source.place: Corollary 1.39 and Proposition 1.26, printed pp.13--18; Proposition 1.52, p.21; quotient Theorems 5.14, 5.28 and Proposition 5.29, pp.100--105; Exercise 5-5(a),(b) and Exercise 5-6, printed p.122 (in 5-6 normality of N is needed). Agent-formulated normal-kernel factorization and equivariance consequence. Smoothness of the torsor uses Stacks Tag 02VL (smoothness fpqc local on the base). No claim that Conrad proves this factorization verbatim.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup], $N$ is a closed subgroup of $H$ with $N(R)=\ker q(R)$ for every $k$-algebra $R$. It is normal since $q(hnh^{-1})=q(h)1q(h)^{-1}=1$. Write $N=\operatorname{Spec}B$, so $L=\operatorname{Spec}(B/\sqrt{0})$ by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Both are affine of finite type: on the affine $H$, their coordinate algebras are quotients of the finitely generated algebra $k[H]$, generated by the images of its generators. Their underlying spaces coincide, since every prime contains every nilpotent; hence $\dim L=\dim N$. The algebraically closed field $k$ is perfect: in characteristic $p$, the polynomial $T^p-c$ has a root for every $c\in k$.

source.place: Corollary 1.39, printed p.18; kernel normality before Theorem 5.14, p.102; Exercise 5-5, p.122.

proof.text: The product $L\times_k L$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor], [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff]. Any homomorphism from $B$ to a reduced ring kills $\sqrt0$, since the image of a nilpotent is nilpotent. Thus multiplication $L\times L\to N$, inversion $L\to N$ and the identity $\operatorname{Spec}k\to N$ factor uniquely through $L$. Their group identities follow after composing with the closed inclusion $L\to N$, which is injective on every test algebra's points. This constructs the closed subgroup $L$, not just its geometric points.

source.place: Proposition 1.38 and Corollary 1.39, printed p.18; Stacks Tag 047R, groupoids-lemma-reduced-subgroup-scheme-perfect (argument supplied).

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect] to the reduced finite-type scheme $L$ over the perfect field $k$. It is geometrically reduced. The group scheme just constructed is locally of finite type, so [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth] makes $L$ smooth. Also $H$ is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], applied to its structure morphism and its sole fibre. The affine product $H\times_k L$ is reduced by the same tensor-product and affine-spectrum results as in step 2. Conjugation $H\times L\to H$ factors through $N$, because $N$ is a scheme-theoretic normal kernel. Its pullback on $k[N]$ kills nilpotents, hence it factors through $L$. Consequently $hL(R)h^{-1}\subseteq L(R)$ for all $h\in H(R)$ and all $R$; replacing $h$ by $h^{-1}$ gives equality. This proves scheme-theoretic normality without a connectedness assumption on $L$.

source.place: Proposition 1.26, p.13; Corollary 1.39, p.18; normal-kernel case of Exercise 5-6, p.122. Geometric reduction: Stacks Tag 020I, varieties-lemma-perfect-reduced; smoothness Tags 047P and 047N.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] for $L\triangleleft H$. It gives the affine finite-type group $P=H/L$, the fppf coset-sheaf interpretation, the faithfully flat finitely presented quotient $a$, its kernel $L$, and the specified isomorphism $(h,l)\mapsto(h,hl)$ from $H\times L$ to $H\times_P H$. It also gives smoothness of $P$. The connected $H$ has its identity $k$-point, so [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] makes $H$ geometrically connected; the quotient theorem then makes $P$ geometrically connected, in particular connected.

source.place: Propositions 5.24--5.29, pp.104--105; Proposition 5.59, p.114; Section 5(j), pp.116--118.

proof.text: The base change of $a$ along itself is, by its torsor isomorphism, $H\times_k L\to H$, $(h,l)\mapsto h$; the swap of the two factors of $H\times_PH$ exchanges its two projections, so either projection may be used. This is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] applied to the smooth structure map of $L$. Since $a$ is faithfully flat and quasi-compact (indeed finitely presented), [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent] implies that $a$ is smooth. Thus its asserted smooth fppf torsor properties all hold, even if $L$ is disconnected.

source.place: Corollary 5.27, p.105; Proposition 7.15, p.142. Smooth descent: Stacks Tag 02VL, descent-lemma-descending-property-smooth; smooth base change Tag 01VB.

proof.text: For clarity identify the target $J$ with $H/N$. Let $c:H\to Q=H/N$ be the quotient given by [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry]. The universal property [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-group-quotient-universal], applied first to $c$ and then to the given $q$, produces homomorphisms $u:Q\to J$ and $v:J\to Q$ with $uc=q$ and $vq=c$, because their scheme-theoretic kernels are both $N$. Uniqueness in that property yields $vu=1_Q$ and $uv=1_J$: both composites agree with the identity after $c$, respectively after $q$. Hence $u$ identifies $Q$ with $J$, with the actual given map $q$ as quotient. Apply the same universal property to $a$ and $q$; since $q$ kills $L$, there is a unique homomorphism $b:P\to J$ with $ba=q$.

source.place: Theorem 5.13, p.101; Proposition 5.29, p.105. Both quotient universal properties are applied to affine finite-type groups.

proof.text: Now apply [lem-sfb-nested-homogeneous-quotient-geometry] to $L\subseteq N\subseteq H$. Step 1 gives the required equality of topological dimensions. Therefore its canonical map $H/L\to H/N$ is finite and faithfully flat. The single map $a$ is an fpqc covering of $P$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: it is flat and surjective, and for an affine open $V\subseteq P$ the open $a^{-1}(V)$ of the Noetherian scheme $H$ is a finite union of affine opens whose images cover $V$. By the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], two morphisms out of $P$ agreeing after $a$ are equal. Since $u\pi a=uc=q=ba$, the map $\pi$ equals $b$ after the identification $u$ of step 6. The correspondence clause of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] applied to $a$ and the pair $1\triangleleft\ker b\subseteq P$ identifies the corresponding quotient with $N/L$: more explicitly $a^{-1}(\ker b)=\ker(ba)=N$, and the inverse-image subgroup correspondence gives $\ker b=N/L$. No smoothness of $N$ has been assumed.

source.place: Proposition 7.15 and Remark 7.16(b), pp.142--143; Theorem 5.55, p.113. Use the direction of the Cartesian square and Remark 7.16, not the reversed arrow in the second sentence of 7.15.

proof.text: Let $\Omega/k$ be algebraically closed. The base change $a_\Omega$ is smooth and surjective by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Its fibre over any $p\in P(\Omega)$ is smooth and nonempty, hence has an $\Omega$-point by [lem-pc-rational-points-dense]. Thus choose lifts $h_1,h_2\in H(\Omega)$ of any $p_1,p_2$ with $b(p_1)=b(p_2)$. Then $h_1^{-1}h_2\in N(\Omega)=L(\Omega)$, since every ring map from $k[N]$ to the field $\Omega$ kills nilpotents. Therefore $p_1=p_2$ by the coset criterion. For any field $K$ and two $K$-points over the same point of $J$, pass to an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $K$; equality there implies equality over $K$, since $P$ is affine and $K\to\Omega$ is injective. This proves the field-point criterion of [def-weil-radicial-morphism], so $b$ is radicial.

source.place: Exercise 5-5(a), p.122, and Remark 7.16(c), p.143, with geometric-point argument made explicit; Stacks Tag 01S4, morphisms-lemma-universally-injective.

proof.text: Suppose $A$ acts as stated. Equivariance of $q$ makes the action restrict to $A\times N\to N$, since it preserves the identity of $J$. The smooth $A$ is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. The affine $A\times L$ is reduced by the perfect-field tensor and affine-spectrum results, so its map to $N$ kills nilpotents and factors through $L$. Inverses in $A$ show equality of the subgroup after every base change. Thus the action preserves $L$ scheme-theoretically.

source.place: Proposition 1.38 argument, p.18, applied to the action instead of multiplication; Exercise 5-6, p.122 (normality of the original kernel is in force).

proof.text: For a test scheme $T$, $t\in A(T)$ and $p\in P(T)$, the base change $T'=H\times_{P,p}T\to T$ of the fpqc covering $a$ of step 7 is an fpqc covering by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change], and on it $p$ lifts tautologically to the first projection $h\in H(T')$. Define $t\cdot p=a(t\cdot h)$. Two lifts differ by right multiplication by $l\in L$, and the automorphism action gives $t\cdot(hl)=(t\cdot h)(t\cdot l)$ with $t\cdot l\in L$ by step 9. Thus the definitions agree on overlaps. For two such covers $T',T''$, the projection $T'\times_TT''\to T'$ is again an fpqc covering by the same lemma, so equalities of morphisms descend along it and then along $T'\to T$; [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] glues the values uniquely. The rule is natural in $T$, so [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] gives $A\times P\to P$. After locally lifting $p,p'$ (on the common refinement of their covers), the equations $t\cdot(pp')=(t\cdot p)(t\cdot p')$, $1\cdot p=p$ and $(tt')\cdot p=t\cdot(t'\cdot p)$ follow from those on $H$; equality descends by uniqueness. The element $t^{-1}$ supplies the inverse automorphism. The definition proves equivariance of $a$. Finally $b(t\cdot a(h))=q(t\cdot h)=t\cdot q(h)=t\cdot b(a(h))$ locally, so uniqueness of descent proves equivariance of $b$ globally.
